The season began on 27 March and ended on 5 December 2021.{{cite web|url=https://tntsports.cl/nacional/El-Campeonato-Nacional-2021-tiene-fecha-de-inicio-20210214-0008.html|title=El Campeonato Nacional 2021 tiene fecha de inicio|language=es|publisher=TNT Sports|date=14 February 2021|access-date=19 February 2021|archive-date=27 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220227085036/https://tntsports.cl/nacional/El-Campeonato-Nacional-2021-tiene-fecha-de-inicio-20210214-0008.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite web |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/aprobado-la-segunda-no-tendra-un-solo-ascenso-directo-a-la-primera-b/3EN6TAEJJZBCNEXMQEMZXHKAM4/|title=Aprobado: la Segunda no tendrá un solo ascenso directo a la Primera B|language=es|publisher=La Tercera|date=2 March 2021|access-date=3 March 2021}} [[Club Deportivo Universidad Católica|Universidad Católica]] were the defending champions, and won their fourth straight title in the competition, and sixteenth overall, after a 3–0 away win over [[Everton de Viña del Mar|Everton]] on 4 December 2021, the last matchday of the season.{{cite web |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/tetracampeones-la-uc-es-la-duena-absoluta-del-futbol-chileno/GWF3E3HBIJGMLDSQ3OSHCF2XGQ/|title=Tetracampeones: la UC es la dueña absoluta del fútbol chileno|language=es|publisher=La Tercera|date=4 December 2021|access-date=5 December 2021}} ==Format== In early February 2021, several bodies floated format proposals for the 2021 season, considering that the 2020 and 2021 editions of both the [[Copa Chile]] and [[Supercopa de Chile]] still needed to be played. [[Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional|ANFP]] considered playing a tournament with two stages, starting from late March. In the first stage, the 17 teams would play each other in a single round-robin tournament with the teams being split for the second stage in two groups: the top eight teams would play against each other for the championship, four Copa Libertadores berths and two Copa Sudamericana ones, while the remaining nine teams would play to avoid relegation, with the top team of that group also qualifying for the Copa Sudamericana. Three teams would be relegated: two teams directly and another one in a play-off. Meanwhile, the players union Sifup proposed to play a double round-robin tournament from April to December with two relegations, the 2020 Copa Chile in the first semester of 2021 and a league cup involving the Primera División teams in the second semester, with league broadcaster TNT Sports supporting a double round-robin tournament, or two short tournaments with play-offs in case the long tournament proposal was not feasible.{{cite web |url=https://www.adnradio.cl/futbol/2021/02/05/se-comienza-a-planificar-el-torneo-las-propuestas-para-el-proximo-campeonato-nacional-2021.html|title=Solo una rueda y grupos para pelear el campeonato y el descenso: Las propuestas para el próximo torneo chileno|language=es|publisher=ADN Radio|date=5 February 2021|access-date=19 February 2021}} On 2 March 2021, ANFP's Council of Presidents voted to approve the format for the season. It was eventually decided to play a double round-robin tournament with the top three teams after 34 rounds qualifying for the Copa Libertadores, with a fourth berth being awarded to the [[2021 Copa Chile]] champions. The teams placed from fourth to seventh place will qualify for the Copa Sudamericana, while the bottom two teams were relegated to [[Primera B de Chile|Primera B]], with the team placed third-from-bottom playing a double-legged play-off against the winners of the Primera B play-offs.{{cite web |url=https://www.latercera.com/la-tercera-pm/noticia/guia-para-entender-el-torneo-nacional-2021-ascensos-descensos-cupos-internacionales-y-mas/YGHVMFRS4FDI5OVBUPVZMNKT34/|title=Guía para entender el torneo nacional 2021: Ascensos, descensos, cupos internacionales y más|language=es|publisher=La Tercera|date=26 February 2021|access-date=3 March 2021}} ==Teams== 17 teams took part in the league in this season, down by one from the previous season: 15 teams from the 2020 tournament, plus the [[2020 Primera B de Chile|2020 Primera B]] champions [[Ñublense]] and [[Deportes Melipilla]], winners of the [[2020 Primera B de Chile#Promotion play-off|Primera B promotion play-offs]]. Ñublense returned to the top flight after five and a half years, while Deportes Melipilla played in Primera División after 13 years.{{cite web|url=https://www.anfp.cl/noticia/36665/nublense-es-campeon-y-vuelve-a-primera-division-tras-mas-de-5-anos-en-el-ascenso|title=Ñublense es campeón y vuelve a Primera División tras más de 5 años en el ascenso|language=es|publisher=ANFP|date=9 January 2021|access-date=19 February 2021|archive-date=6 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206211554/https://www.anfp.cl/noticia/36665/nublense-es-campeon-y-vuelve-a-primera-division-tras-mas-de-5-anos-en-el-ascenso|url-status=dead}}{{cite web |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/melipilla-asciende-a-primera-division-tras-una-infartante-definicion-a-penales/75ALXAWI55BGVPHEYO5LSGGFVY/|title=Melipilla asciende a Primera División tras una infartante definición a penales|language=es|publisher=La Tercera|date=7 February 2021|access-date=19 February 2021}} Both promoted teams replaced [[Coquimbo Unido]], [[Deportes Iquique]], and [[C.D.
